plan.approach:
**Real-time 3D in three.js/WebGL2, rendered headless through SwiftShader, split into a 3D world layer and a deterministic Canvas2D overlay layer.**

I probed the box before deciding. Headless Chromium exposes real WebGL2 via ANGLE→Vulkan→SwiftShader (Subzero JIT). A 1920×1080 scene with 20k instanced shadow-receiving meshes, a 2048² PCF shadow map and ACES tonemapping renders in **29.6 ms/frame**. That single number decides the architecture: we are not restricted to a toy renderer. A still capture that accumulates 24–48 jittered frames (for TAA, bokeh DOF and motion blur) costs 0.7–1.5 s. So the capture path can be far more expensive than the play path, and the frame a critic screenshots can carry AAA post that no software rasterizer could sustain at 60 fps.

Second decisive measurement: **the bar panels are only 310–376 px tall.** At that size, photoreal micro-detail is not what wins the blind A/B — *silhouette, value structure, color, rim-light placement, atmospheric depth, composition, and typography* are. We cannot out-render an AI photoreal image on skin pores. We can absolutely match and beat it on staging, grade, particle language and lettering. So the decomposition deliberately over-invests in cinematography, lighting, VFX and type, and treats character fidelity as three separate convergeable problems (geometry, materials, pose) rather than one impossible one.

Third: only DejaVu/Liberation/FreeSans exist on this box — nothing resembling the hand-lettered brush-italic in every callout and menu header. Custom vector lettering is therefore not a flourish, it is a required piece, and it's one of the highest-probability wins in the whole set because 2D type can be matched *exactly*.

Layering: 3D world (three.js) beneath, a fixed 1920×1080 Canvas2D overlay above. Canvas2D — not DOM/CSS — because it is deterministic (no font/layout drift between runs), pixel-exact, and supports the bevels, gradient maps, roughened edges and grain the bar's UI needs. Menus are overlay screens drawn over an optional 3D backdrop, so `title`, `team_select`, `uniform` and `playcall_def` each become a small, self-contained, near-pixel-matchable target.

Parallelism is enforced by a frozen foundation that ships a registry, a rig spec, and **working fallbacks for every contract**. On round 1 every builder can run, render and screenshot in isolation because nothing they depend on is missing — it's just stubbed. Pieces own directories, never files outside them. Shared data (rig bones, shot spec schema, texture helpers, RNG) lives only in foundation and is never edited after t=0.

Each piece gets an **isolation scene it alone owns** (registered through `registerIsoShot`) plus at least one hero panel it shares. That is what makes the critic loop work: a blind critic can pose exactly this piece's contribution, screenshot it, and score it against one named bar panel or one named quality, without the piece's weaknesses being masked or its strengths hidden by a neighbor.
plan.stack:
**Runtime:** three.js r0.185.1 + Vite 8 (vanilla ES2022 modules, no framework, no TypeScript). WebGL2 forward renderer, ACES filmic tonemapping, PCF shadows, `EffectComposer` + custom passes from `three/examples/jsm/postprocessing`. All assets procedural: textures baked at boot into `OffscreenCanvas`/`DataTexture` via a shared `texlab` (fBm/worley/curl noise, height→normal, gradient ramps, decal compositing). Zero network at runtime, zero CDN, zero binary art assets.

**Two layers:** (1) `<canvas id="gl">` — the three.js world. (2) `<canvas id="ui">` — a fixed 1920×1080 Canvas2D overlay for HUD, callouts and all menu screens. Both composited by CSS stacking; both captured in one Playwright screenshot.

**Determinism.** No `Math.random`, `Date.now`, or `performance.now` anywhere under `src/pieces/` — enforced by `scripts/lint-determinism.mjs`, which fails the build. All randomness flows from `makeRng(seed)` (mulberry32) seeded off the URL. All animation is a **pure function of simulated time `t`**, never wall clock. The sim advances by fixed 1/120 s steps from `t=0` to the requested `t`, so `?t=2.6` is byte-reproducible.

**Deterministic still capture.** `scripts/shoot.mjs` (Playwright 1.56.1, already global at `/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright`) launches Chromium with `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader --no-sandbox --force-device-scale-factor=1`, viewport 1920×1080, `deviceScaleFactor:1`. It builds (`vite build`) if `dist/` is stale, `npm ci`s if `node_modules/` is missing, serves `dist/` on 127.0.0.1:5178, navigates to the scene URL, then waits on `window.__BLITZ_READY__ === true`.

Readiness is engine-driven, not timer-driven: the engine renders `warmup` frames (default 8) so every lazy texture bake, shader compile and skinning upload has landed, then runs `accum` (default 32) sub-pixel-jittered accumulation passes that resolve TAA, bokeh DOF and motion blur into a float accumulation target, then resolves, then draws the Canvas2D overlay, *then* sets `__BLITZ_READY__` and `document.documentElement.dataset.blitzReady="1"`. Two runs of the same URL produce identical PNGs.

**A/B composite without ImageMagick/PIL** (neither exists on this box): `scripts/compare.mjs` screenshots a foundation-owned `compare.html?panel=truck&shot=shots/truck.png`, which lays the bar panel and our frame side by side **scaled to identical 720 px height** (critical — bar panels are only ~340 px tall, so unmatched scaling would confound the judgement), with a labelled gutter and an optional wipe. Output is a single PNG the critic reads.

**Quality modes:** `?quality=capture` (SSAA 1.5×, 32-frame accum, 4096² shadows, full post chain, 64k particles) vs `?quality=live` (1× , no accum, 2048² shadows, reduced post) so the game stays interactive while stills stay maximal.

foundationSpec.summary: The foundation builds a runnable, screenshottable skeleton with WORKING FALLBACKS for every contract, so all 16 pieces can be built, run and captured in parallel on round 1 with nothing missing. It owns every shared file; after t=0 it is FROZEN and no builder may edit any file listed here. It also creates one placeholder `src/pieces/<id>/index.js` per piece (a no-op that registers nothing) — those 16 files are handed off at t=0 and belong exclusively to their piece thereafter. Deliverables: (a) Vite+three app with a 3D canvas and a fixed 1920x1080 Canvas2D overlay; (b) a registry every piece plugs into; (c) a frozen skeleton/rig spec so geometry, materials and posing can be built by three different agents without touching each other; (d) a ShotSpec schema and a world assembler that turns a ShotSpec into a rendered frame; (e) procedural texture helpers (fBm/worley/curl noise, height-to-normal, ramps, decal compositing) so pieces don't each reinvent them; (f) a seeded-RNG module plus a determinism linter that FAILS the build on Math.random/Date.now/performance.now under src/pieces; (g) a bulletproof Playwright capture script and a zero-dependency side-by-side compare tool; (h) the live progress page. Fallbacks must be deliberately PLAIN (untextured grey capsules, system-font text, flat lighting) so a critic can never mistake a fallback for a piece's real output. Foundation must verify `node scripts/shoot.mjs --all` produces a PNG for every registered scene before handing off.
foundationSpec.contracts:
ALL of the following live in foundation files and are FROZEN after t=0.

=== 1. REGISTRY (src/foundation/registry.js) ===
`export const REG = { world:{stadium,lighting,turf,anatomy,uniform,pose,fx}, ui:{hud,callout,teamSelect,uniformScreen,playcall,title}, cinema, brand, faces, sim, isoShots:{} }`
Registration fns (a later call overwrites the fallback):
`registerWorld(slot, impl)` slot in `'stadium'|'lighting'|'turf'|'anatomy'|'uniform'|'pose'|'fx'`
`registerUI(slot, impl)` slot in `'hud'|'callout'|'teamSelect'|'uniformScreen'|'playcall'|'title'`
`registerCinema(impl)` / `registerBrand(impl)` / `registerFaces(impl)` / `registerSim(impl)`
`registerIsoShot(sceneId, shotSpec)` — a piece's own capture scene; foundation's scene resolver checks REG.isoShots FIRST, then cinema.shots. This is what keeps per-piece capture scenes file-disjoint.
`src/pieces/index.js` statically imports all 16 `./<id>/index.js` in fixed alphabetical order; each piece's index.js calls its register(s) as an import side effect and exports nothing.

=== 2. CTX — passed to every build/update ===
`ctx = { THREE, renderer, scene, camera, rng, texlab, brand, faces, quality:'capture'|'live', t, seed, shot, W:1920, H:1080 }`

=== 3. WORLD SLOT INTERFACES ===
`stadium : { build(ctx) -> THREE.Object3D, update(t, ctx) }`
`lighting: { build(ctx) -> { group:Object3D, key:DirectionalLight, env:Texture|null, exposure:number, applyToRenderer(renderer) }, update(t, ctx) }`
`turf    : { build(ctx) -> Object3D, addDivot(x,z,dirX,dirZ,strength), addCleatMark(x,z,rotY,depth), addSkid(x0,z0,x1,z1,w), reset(), update(t,ctx) }`  // field coords: origin at midfield, +X toward the right sideline, +Z toward the near sideline (camera side), 1 unit = 1 metre; field is 91.44 x 48.8 with endzones at |X| > 45.72
`anatomy : { build(ctx, {archetype:'qb'|'skill'|'lineman'|'lb', heightM, massKg, seed}) -> Actor, setMaterials(actor, matSet) }`
  `Actor = { root:Object3D, mesh:SkinnedMesh, skeleton:Skeleton, sockets:{head,rightHand,leftHand,chest,hips,rightFoot,leftFoot}, slotOrder:string[] }`
`uniform : { materials(ctx, teamId, variant:'home'|'away'|'alt1'|'alt2'|'throwback', {number,name,dirt:0..1,wet:0..1}) -> matSet, screen: UIScreen }`
  `matSet` keys EXACTLY: `skin, undershirt, jersey, pants, sock, cleat, glove, helmetShell, facemask, visor, pad, towel`
`pose    : { list() -> string[], apply(skeleton, poseId, phase:0..1, seed) -> void, velocityHint(poseId, phase) -> Vector3 }`
`fx      : { build(ctx) -> Object3D, emitImpact(pos, dir, power, kind:'hit'|'truck'|'catch'|'cleat'), ball(ctx) -> {mesh, setFlame(0..1), setSpin(rps)}, update(t, ctx) }`

=== 4. RIG SPEC (src/foundation/rig.js) — FROZEN BONE LIST ===
Exactly 26 bones, canonical A-pose, +Y up, +Z forward, metres, hip origin at y=0.98 for a 1.88 m player:
`root, hips, spine01, spine02, chest, neck, head, clavicle_L/R, upperarm_L/R, forearm_L/R, hand_L/R, thigh_L/R, shin_L/R, foot_L/R, toe_L/R`
Exports `BONES` (ordered names), `REST` (rest transforms), `makeSkeleton()`, `SOCKETS`, and `PROPORTIONS[archetype]` (limb-length multipliers, shoulder width, neck girth, pad bulk factor). anatomy skins to THIS skeleton; pose only writes bone quaternions/positions; uniform only writes materials. This 3-way split is what makes those three pieces file-disjoint.

=== 5. SHOTSPEC (src/foundation/contracts.js) ===
`{ id, aspect:1.777, camera:{pos:[x,y,z], target:[x,y,z], fov, roll}, lens:{fStop, focusDist, bokehScale, shutter}, exposure, tod:'night', weather:{rain,lightning,haze}, actors:[{team, variant, number, name, archetype, pose, phase, pos:[x,y,z], rotY, scale, airborne}], ball:{pos:[x,y,z], rotQ, flame:0..1, visible}, fx:[{kind, pos:[x,y,z], dir:[x,y,z], power, age}], turfDamage:[{type,x,z,rot,strength}], hud:{visible, clock:':15', quarter:2, down:2, dist:'2ND', yards:'250', teamA:'NYC', teamB:'CHI', scoreA:22, scoreB:14, turbo:0.62, momentumA:0.5, momentumB:0.3}, callout:{visible, line1:'MID-AIR', line2:'MURDER!', pts:250, accent:'red'|'gold', age}, ui:{screen:null|'title'|'teamSelect'|'uniform'|'playcall', state:{}} }`

=== 6. WORLD ASSEMBLER (src/foundation/world.js) ===
`buildFromShot(shot, ctx)` runs in FIXED order: turf.build -> stadium.build -> lighting.build -> for each actor { anatomy.build, uniform.materials, anatomy.setMaterials, pose.apply } -> fx.build + fx.ball -> apply shot.turfDamage via turf.addDivot/addCleatMark -> cinema.applyShot(camera, shot, t) -> cinema.buildPost(...). Then per frame: update all, render post chain, then overlay.

=== 7. OVERLAY + UI SCREENS (src/foundation/overlay.js) ===
A 1920x1080 Canvas2D context, always that logical size regardless of viewport (CSS-scaled). Foundation calls, in order: `REG.ui.hud.draw(c2d, t, shot.hud, uiCtx)`, `REG.ui.callout.draw(c2d, t, shot.callout, uiCtx)`, and if `shot.ui.screen` the matching screen's `draw(c2d, t, shot.ui.state, uiCtx)`.
`UIScreen = { draw(c2d, t, state, ui) }`; `ui = { W:1920, H:1080, faces, brand, safe:{l:48,t:36,r:48,b:36}, rng, texlab, px(n) }`

=== 8. FACES (src/foundation/typeface.js) — vector type engine + FALLBACK face ===
`faces = { measure(text, faceName, sizePx, opts) -> {w,h,ascent}, path(text, faceName, sizePx, opts) -> Path2D, draw(c2d, text, x, y, {face, size, align:'left'|'center'|'right', baseline, tracking, slant, fill, stroke}) -> {w,h} }`
Face names any consumer may request: `'blitz-brush'` (hand-lettered bold italic display), `'blitz-block'` (condensed squarish HUD/label sans), `'blitz-num'` (tall gold numerals), `'blitz-techno'` (TURBO / tech labels). Foundation's fallback renders all four with system `italic 900 Liberation Sans` so nothing is ever blank. Glyph data format is a frozen JSON schema: `{unitsPerEm, glyphs:{ 'A': {adv, cmds:[['M',x,y],['C',...],['L',...],['Z']] } }, kern:{}}`.

=== 9. BRAND ===
`brand = { teams:[Team], byId(id), crest(id, sizePx) -> HTMLCanvasElement (cached), wordmark(c2d, id, box, opts), skyline(c2d, cityId, box, opts), leagueMark(c2d, box), blitzLogo(c2d, box, opts) }`
`Team = { id:'NYC', city:'NEW YORK', name:'STRYKERS', abbr:'NYC', colors:{primary,secondary,accent,metal,helmet}, stats:{speed:0..1, hitPower:0..1, turbo:0..1} }`
Frozen roster ids: `NYC, CHI, DAL, LA, SEA, MIA, BAL, PHI`. Fictional only. No real NFL shield, no real team marks — foundation's `leagueMark` fallback draws a plain chevron badge.

=== 10. SIM ===
`sim = { create(seed, opts) -> state, step(state, dt) -> void, seekTo(state, t) -> void, snapshot(state) -> {actors:[ShotActor], ball:{...}, hud:{...}, events:[{kind,pos,power,t}]} }`
The `live_play` scene builds a shot by calling `sim.seekTo(state, t)` then `sim.snapshot(state)` and feeding the result straight into `buildFromShot`.

=== 11. TEXLAB (src/foundation/texlab.js) ===
`{ noise2, noise3, fbm2, fbm3, worley2, curl3, ridged2, canvas(w,h) -> {cv,ctx}, toTexture(cv, {srgb,wrap,aniso}), heightToNormal(cv, strength) -> Texture, ramp(stops) -> (t)->[r,g,b], dataTexture(fn, w, h, {float}), blueNoise(size), cached(key, fn) }`

=== 12. RNG ===
`{ makeRng(seed) -> ()=>0..1, hash(...ints), pick(rng, arr), gauss(rng), seedFromString(s) }`

=== 13. URL PARAMS (src/foundation/params.js) ===
`scene` (required), `seed` (default 7), `t` (default 0, seconds), `w`/`h` (default 1920/1080), `quality` (`capture`|`live`, default `live`; shoot.mjs always sends `capture`), `accum` (default 32), `warmup` (default 8), `hud` (`1`|`0`), `ui` (`1`|`0`), `layer` (`all`|`gl`|`overlay` — lets a critic capture the overlay alone on transparent/grey), `variant` (free string a piece may use for its own iso scene sub-poses), `debug` (`1` draws a safe-area/measure grid).

=== 14. FILE OWNERSHIP RULE ===
Every piece writes ONLY inside `/home/user/nflblitz/src/pieces/<piece-id>/`. No exceptions. Pieces IMPORT from `src/foundation/*` and may import another piece's public export via the registry (`REG.faces`, `REG.brand`) but must NEVER import another piece's files directly and must NEVER edit any file outside their own directory. Screenshots go to `/home/user/nflblitz/shots/<piece-id>/`, which is piece-owned. Progress events are appended (never rewritten) via `node scripts/log-event.mjs`.
foundationSpec.captureProtocol:
ONE command produces a PNG. It self-heals: runs `npm ci` if node_modules is missing, `vite build` if dist/ is stale, starts a static server on 127.0.0.1:5178, drives Playwright, and tears down.

  cd /home/user/nflblitz && node scripts/shoot.mjs --scene=<sceneId> --out=shots/<piece-id>/<name>.png

Full flag set:
  --scene=<id>      required; any id in REG.isoShots or cinema.shots (see `node scripts/shoot.mjs --list`)
  --seed=7          RNG seed (default 7)
  --t=0             simulated seconds; animation is a pure function of t (default 0)
  --variant=<str>   piece-defined sub-pose within its own iso scene
  --w=1920 --h=1080 capture size (default 1920x1080)
  --layer=all|gl|overlay   capture both layers, 3D only, or the Canvas2D overlay only
  --hud=0|1 --ui=0|1       force HUD / menu-screen visibility
  --out=<path>      output PNG
  --all             every registered scene -> shots/all/<sceneId>.png
  --piece=<id>      every scene that piece declares -> shots/<id>/
  --list            print all registered scene ids and exit

Underlying URL (a critic can also open this in their own Playwright session):
  http://127.0.0.1:5178/?scene=<id>&seed=7&t=0&quality=capture&accum=32&warmup=8&w=1920&h=1080

READINESS — never sleep, always wait on this:
  await page.waitForFunction('window.__BLITZ_READY__===true', {timeout:240000})
The engine sets it only after warmup frames, all `accum` jittered accumulation passes, the post resolve, AND the Canvas2D overlay draw have completed. `window.__BLITZ_STATS__` then holds `{ms, frames, drawCalls, tris, sceneId, seed, t}` for a sanity check. Chromium must be launched with `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader --no-sandbox --force-device-scale-factor=1` and `deviceScaleFactor:1`.

SIDE-BY-SIDE AGAINST THE BAR (no ImageMagick or PIL on this box — this uses Chromium):
  node scripts/compare.mjs --panel=truck --shot=shots/pose-animation/truck.png --out=shots/pose-animation/cmp-truck.png
It screenshots `compare.html`, which scales BOTH images to an identical 720 px height (bar panels are only ~310-376 px tall; unmatched scaling would confound the judgement), labels them BAR / OURS, and butts them together with a 16 px gutter. Add `--wipe=0.5` for a single-image split composite, or `--crop=hud|callout|face` to compare a named region.

Typical critic loop for a piece:
  node scripts/shoot.mjs --piece=<piece-id>
  node scripts/compare.mjs --panel=<barPanel> --shot=shots/<piece-id>/<scene>.png --out=shots/<piece-id>/cmp.png
  Read shots/<piece-id>/cmp.png, score it, name ONE gap
  node scripts/log-event.mjs --piece=<id> --round=<n> --event=verdict --score=<0-100> --gap="..." --shot=<path>

SANITY GATE before any verdict: `node scripts/lint-determinism.mjs` must pass, and shooting the same scene twice must yield byte-identical PNGs. If it doesn't, that non-determinism IS the finding.

pieces.name: Night Stadium Bowl, Crowd & Boards
pieces.brief: Build the entire stadium that surrounds the field: a full lower bowl, mezzanine and upper deck of raked seating that wraps 360 degrees, tunnel mouths, sideline benches, camera scaffolds, goalposts, pylons, sideline photographers, and a roof/rigging truss with light banks hanging from it. Populate the stands with a dense crowd — tens of thousands — using instanced geometry with per-instance color, height and slouch variation from seeded RNG; the bar's stands read as a warm brown-and-dark speckle with scattered white camera-flash sparkles and phone screens, NOT as uniform noise, so bias colors toward team palettes near the field and add a sparse, seeded set of tiny emissive flash points. Add a huge jumbotron showing a live-looking feed, LED ribbon boards running the fascia with scrolling fictional sponsor text, and end-zone video walls. The whole thing must sit far enough back and be atmospheric enough that heavy depth-of-field and haze dissolve it into a glowing backdrop rather than a hard model. Export a `stadiumHeat(x,z)` helper other pieces can ignore. Field coordinate frame is fixed by the foundation. No real NFL branding anywhere — all sponsor and league marks fictional. Judge it on how the background reads at panel scale.
pieces.judgeOn: At matched 720px height against panel-qb_dropback: does the bowl have the same layered depth (lower bowl / dark mid band / bright upper ring of lights)? Is the crowd a believable dense mass with warm speckle and scattered flash points rather than obvious repeated blobs or flat noise? Are ribbon boards and the jumbotron present and correctly glowing? Does the bowl silhouette read as an enclosed NFL-scale stadium and not an open field? Correct scale relationship between players and the stands?
pieces.captureScene: node scripts/shoot.mjs --piece=stadium-bowl  (owns iso scenes: iso_stadium_wide, iso_stadium_crowd, iso_stadium_boards; also appears in qb_dropback, catch, truck)

pieces.name: Night Lighting Rig, Volumetrics & Storm
pieces.brief: Own every photon. Build the night stadium light rig: banks of hot practical lights on the roof truss that produce visible flare-cored sources, a key that rakes players from behind-left to create the hard white rim on shoulder pads and helmets seen in every action panel, a cool blue-violet fill from the sky, and warm bounce from the field. Then the atmosphere: volumetric god-rays / light shafts descending from the banks through haze — this is the single most distinctive feature of the bar art. Implement them as a raymarched screen-space or camera-facing billboard-shaft system with depth-aware occlusion so players carve shadows into the shafts. Add graded exponential height fog, drifting haze/steam, faint rain streaks, and a storm sky dome with layered scrolling cloud noise plus a seeded lightning system (multi-branch bolt geometry, a full-scene flash burst, and a brief exposure bump). Provide an IBL environment map baked procedurally from the sky + light banks so materials get real specular. Deliver a `night`, `storm` and `flash` preset. Everything must be a pure function of `t`.
pieces.judgeOn: Named quality: 'volumetric night stadium lighting'. Are there visible, believably occluded light shafts? Do the three mannequins in iso_light carry a hard bright rim on the upper-left/back edge with the front dropping into deep shadow, matching the bar's rim-light language? Is the overall value structure correct — near-black midtones, blown highlights only at light sources and rims? Is the sky a moody purple-black storm with real cloud structure, and does lightning read as a branching bolt plus a scene-wide flash? No flat/even ambient lighting.
pieces.captureScene: node scripts/shoot.mjs --piece=night-lighting  (owns iso_light, iso_shafts, iso_storm, iso_lightning; also appears in midair_hit, leveler)

pieces.name: Turf Shader, Field Paint & Damage
pieces.brief: Own the ground plane. Build a turf material that survives a low raking camera: per-blade or shell-based detail near the camera fading to a tiled anisotropic material at distance, with mow-stripe banding, a wet specular sheen (the bar's field is glossy and reflects the light banks), and darkened saturated color under moisture. Layer on field paint driven by a baked 4K paint texture: yard lines every 5 yards, hash marks, yard numerals at 10-yard intervals with directional arrows, sideline and end-line borders, a painted end zone in team colors with a fictional team wordmark and a midfield crest, plus the blue-and-gold end-zone treatment visible in panel-touchdown. Then damage: a dynamic RGBA damage buffer supporting `addDivot`, `addCleatMark` and `addSkid` that writes displacement + albedo darkening + roughness change, so torn turf shows dark wet soil, scattered loose blades, and boot prints that persist. Cleat marks must be visible under players in every action panel. Provide mud spray color for the FX piece to sample.
pieces.judgeOn: At matched height against panel-truck and panel-touchdown: does the turf read as real wet grass with mow stripes and a specular sheen, not a flat green plane? Are yard lines, hashes, numerals and arrows correct in scale, perspective and slight paint wear? Does the end zone read as a painted colored field with a wordmark? In iso_turf_damage, do divots show dark torn soil with scattered blades, and are cleat marks legible? Does the ground carry the reflected stadium lights the way the bar does?
pieces.captureScene: node scripts/shoot.mjs --piece=turf-field  (owns iso_turf, iso_turf_damage, iso_turf_paint, iso_endzone; also appears in truck, touchdown)

pieces.name: Player Geometry, Pads & Silhouette
pieces.brief: Build the player body — geometry only, no materials, no posing. Produce a `SkinnedMesh` bound to the foundation's frozen 26-bone skeleton, procedurally generated per archetype (`qb`, `skill`, `lineman`, `lb`) with seeded variation in height, mass, limb length and musculature. The bar's players are exaggerated arcade-heroic: enormous shoulder pad flare, tapered V-torso, thick thighs, small waist, big hands. Model the gear as real geometry, because it defines the silhouette: helmet shell with correct dome/jaw profile, a tubular multi-bar facemask, chin strap, visor plane, shoulder pad shells with visible epaulettes and a clavicle gap, back plate, rib pads under the jersey, forearm pads, thigh/knee pad bulges inside the pants, high socks, and cleats with a sole and toe box. Add gloves as separate hand geometry with articulated fingers. Include jersey cloth folds sculpted into the mesh, a slightly untucked hem, and a hanging towel. Provide 2 LODs and clean skin weights so the pose piece can throw the body into a full-extension dive without pinching. Name every material slot exactly as the foundation contract specifies.
pieces.judgeOn: In iso_player (single figure, neutral grey clay material, 3/4 hero framing) and iso_player_silhouette (pure black on white): does the silhouette read instantly as a modern armored football player with heroic arcade proportions — huge shoulder flare, V-taper, thick legs? Is the helmet profile right, with a real multi-bar facemask that reads as tubes and not a flat card? Are pads, gloves, socks and cleats present as geometry? Compare limb proportion and pad bulk against the figure in panel-uniform. No smooth featureless mannequin, no floating gear, no interpenetration.
pieces.captureScene: node scripts/shoot.mjs --piece=player-anatomy  (owns iso_player, iso_player_silhouette, iso_player_lineup, iso_helmet)

pieces.name: Uniform Materials + PICK YOUR UNIFORM Screen
pieces.brief: Two linked deliverables. (1) The material set for every player: jersey with visible knit/mesh weave, dual-layer stretch panels, stitched seams, sublimated team color blocking, sleeve stripes, a tackle-twill number on chest and back with a contrasting outline, a curved nameplate, team crest on the sleeve, and a fictional league mark on the collar — all baked procedurally into albedo/normal/roughness. Plus: helmet shell with deep candy gloss, metallic flake and a clearcoat highlight; matte facemask; tinted visor; leather-and-silicone gloves with a grip pattern; cleats with gloss uppers and matte soles; spandex pants with a sheen; sweat, mud spatter and grass stains driven by a `dirt` and `wet` parameter so late-game players look wrecked like the bar's. Deliver five variants — home, away, alt1, alt2, throwback — for all 8 teams. (2) The PICK YOUR UNIFORM screen: a hero player standing on a slow turntable under a rim-lit studio setup, a giant desaturated team crest watermark behind him at the left, the city/team name stacked below it, a right-hand vertical stack of five bevelled buttons with the selected one outlined in team color, and an 'A SELECT / B BACK' footer with colored button glyphs.

pieces.name: Pose Library & Procedural Animation
pieces.brief: Own how bodies move and hold themselves. Deliver a pose library keyed by id, each a full 26-bone pose evaluated as a function of `phase` 0..1, plus procedural layers (breathing, secondary spine lag, hand/finger shaping, head look-at, foot planting). Required poses, each staged to match a specific bar panel: `qb_dropback_throw` — back to camera, plant foot loaded, ball cocked high behind the ear, off-arm out, torso coiled; `midair_tackle` — tackler fully horizontal in the air, arms wrapping, legs trailing, victim's head snapping back with limbs flailing; `truck_carry` — ball carrier upright and driving, stiff-arm extended into a defender's facemask, off-arm cradling the ball, back leg mid-drive; `leveler_hit` — defender exploding upward through a receiver who is inverted and folding backward; `dive_catch_td` — full horizontal layout extension, ball at fingertips, back arched, legs trailing; `jump_ball_catch` — both hands high above the helmet on the ball at the apex, defender's arm across the chest; plus `idle_ready`, `run_cycle`, `sprint_turbo`, `route_cut`, `stance_offense`, `stance_defense`, `celebrate`. Poses must be extreme and readable in silhouette — this is arcade football, not motion-capture realism. Zero interpenetration; contact points must actually touch.

Score body language against the matching bar panel: does `truck_carry` show a real driving stiff-arm with the defender being displaced? Is `midair_tackle` genuinely horizontal and airborne with the victim's head snapped back? Is `dive_catch_td` a full extension layout with an arched back? Does each pose read as violent and dynamic in silhouette alone? Check contact: hands must land ON the facemask/ball/chest, not through or near them. pieces.name: Camera Staging, Lens & Cinematic Post Stack
pieces.brief: Own the frame. Two halves. (1) Staging: author the ten hero ShotSpecs (`title`, `team_select`, `uniform`, `playcall_def`, `qb_dropback`, `midair_hit`, `truck`, `leveler`, `touchdown`, `catch`) — camera position, target, focal length, roll, subject placement, and the full actor list with poses and phases — so each frame reproduces its bar panel's composition: low sideline camera near turf height, subject filling the left or center third, strong diagonal, deep background compression from a long lens. pieces.name: 7-on-7 Arcade Football Simulation
pieces.brief: Make it an actual game, not a diorama. No flags, no penalties, no out-of-bounds stoppage beyond arcade rules. Body-to-body collision must be resolved so players never interpenetrate, and impacts must call `REG.world.fx.emitImpact` and `REG.world.turf.addDivot` at the right moments. The whole sim must be a deterministic fixed-timestep function of seed and `t`, exposing `seekTo(state, t)` so a critic can screenshot the exact same live play at any moment. Also wire keyboard/gamepad control so a human can play at 60fps in `quality=live`.

plan.progressPageSpec: **File:** `/home/user/nflblitz/progress/index.html` — foundation-owned, frozen, fully self-contained (inline CSS+JS, no CDN, no build step). Served by `node scripts/serve.mjs --progress` on 127.0.0.1:5179 with the repo root as docroot, so `/progress/`, `/shots/` and `/bar/` are all reachable by relative fetch. A second mode, `node scripts/shoot.mjs --progress-snapshot`, inlines the event log as a JS literal and every thumbnail as a data URI into `progress/index.built.html` so the page also works from `file://` or can be published as an Artifact. **Data source — append-only, race-free.** `/home/user/nflblitz/progress/events.jsonl`, one JSON object per line. Builders and critics never rewrite it; they only append via `node scripts/log-event.mjs --piece= --round= --agent=builder|critic|lead --event= [...]`, which does a single `O_APPEND` write so 16 concurrent agents can't corrupt it. Schema: `{ts, round, piece, agent, event, shot?, cmp?, score?, gap?, text?, ms?}` with `event` in `start | build_done | shot | verdict | gap | fixed | note | round_open | round_close`. **What the page shows, top to bottom:** 1. **Header band** — "BLITZ RELOADED / GAUNTLET" in the game's own visual language (dark, red chevron, gold numerals), a big current-round pill, elapsed wall time, and three live counters: pieces building / pieces awaiting verdict / pieces converged (score ≥ 90). 2. **Convergence chart** — one line per piece, score on Y, round on X, drawn as an inline SVG sparkline field with the piece's line colored by its current score (red < 60, amber 60–79, green ≥ 80). This is the at-a-glance answer to "is this working?" — sixteen lines that should all climb right. A dashed horizontal "bar reached" line sits at 90. 3. **The 16-piece board** — the core. A responsive grid of cards, one per piece, ordered by ascending score so the worst work is always on top. Each card carries: the piece name and id; a status dot (idle / building / shooting / judged); a **side-by-side pair** — the bar panel on the left, our latest capture on the right, both at identical height, exactly as the critic sees them; a score ring; and the **latest named gap** verbatim in quotes, since that one sentence is what drives the next round. 4. **Round filmstrip per card** — beneath each pair, a horizontal strip of that piece's captures across every round, oldest to newest, each thumb badged with its round number and score delta (`+14`, `-2`). This is how the page conveys evolution: you scan left to right and literally watch the piece converge on the bar. Hovering a thumb swaps it into the big comparison slot; clicking opens the detail view. 5. **Detail view** (click a card) — full-width overlay: bar panel and our frame at 720px matched height with a **draggable vertical wipe** so you can slide between reference and output, plus toggles for `difference` blend and `50% opacity onion-skin`. Below it, that piece's full event history as a timeline with every gap ever named and whether the next round's score moved. 6. **Live feed** — a reverse-chronological stream of all events across all pieces, color-coded by agent, with critic verdicts expanded and builder notes collapsed. New rows slide in and flash. **Behavior.** Polls `events.jsonl` every 3 s with a `Range` request from the last byte offset, so it only ever pulls new lines — the log can grow to thousands of entries without cost. It diffs by `ts`, animates only what changed, and never resets scroll position or a wipe you're dragging. Screenshot `` tags get a `?v=` cache-buster so a re-shot frame at the same path updates immediately. Missing screenshots render as a labeled placeholder rather than a broken image, so the board is never blank early on. It is theme-aware but commits to the game's dark palette by default, matching the product it is tracking.

Foundation is complete, verified, and frozen.

## HANDOFF — BLITZ RELOADED foundation

**Proof it works** (all run on this box, not stubbed):
- `node scripts/shoot.mjs --all` → **11/11 captures OK** (`shots/all/*.png`: title, team_select, uniform, playcall_def, qb_dropback, truck, midair_hit, leveler, touchdown, catch, live_play). ~20 s/frame at 1920×1080, accum=32, ssaa=1.5, half-float accumulation.
- `shots/foundation.png` captured; shot twice → **byte-identical** (`md5 d96547de45fa9fc684fbfe8a00ea06f1` both times, and again after later engine edits).
- `node scripts/lint-determinism.mjs` → 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `node scripts/compare.mjs` verified in all three modes (side-by-side, `--wipe=0.5`, `--crop=hud`).
- `--piece=menu-title`, `--layer=overlay`, `--layer=gl`, `--hud=0`, `--list` all verified.
- `node tools/progress.mjs` → self-contained `progress/index.html` (3.6 MB, 16 cards, dark+light, detail wipe, live feed). Verified with an empty log, a 4-event log, and a 55-event synthetic log. `node scripts/serve.mjs --progress` returns 200/**206**/200 (Range works).

### How to add a piece
You own **only** `/home/user/nflblitz/src/pieces/<your-id>/` and `shots/<your-id>/`. Your `index.js` is already imported by the frozen `src/pieces/index.js`; do your `register*()` calls as an import side effect. Each placeholder already contains your slot, your register signature, your hero panels, and the exact capture commands — read it first.

```
node scripts/shoot.mjs --piece=<id>
node scripts/compare.mjs --panel=<barPanel> --shot=shots/<id>/<scene>.png --out=shots/<id>/cmp.png
node scripts/lint-determinism.mjs
node scripts/log-event.mjs --piece=<id> --round=<n> --agent=critic --event=verdict --score=<0-100> --gap="..." --shot=<path> --cmp=<path>
```

Register at least one iso scene you alone own: `registerIsoShot('iso:<id>', {piece:'<id>', panel:'truck', camera:{...}, actors:[...], note:'what I claim'})`. The resolver checks `REG.isoShots` before `cinema.shots`.

### The seams
- **rig.js** splits anatomy | pose | uniform three ways: geometry+weights / bone quaternions / materials. 26 bones, all rest quaternions identity and all bone axes world-aligned at bind, so pose authors reason in plain world axes. `REST[name].dir/.len`, `PROPORTIONS[archetype]`, `SOCKETS`, `makeSkeleton()`.
- **ShotSpec** (`contracts.js`) is the only thing that crosses piece boundaries. `makeShot(partial)` fills every field.
- **world.js** runs the fixed assembly order and wraps every slot call — a throwing piece logs to `window.__BLITZ_ERRORS__` and the rest of the frame still renders.
- **overlay.js** is always logical 1920×1080; hard-code those coordinates.
- Field coords: origin midfield, +X right sideline, +Z near sideline (camera side), metres, hips at y=0.98.

### Deviations from spec, and why
1. **`--deterministic-mode` / `--js-flags=--random-seed=7` removed from the Chromium launch.** With them `page.screenshot()` hung >120 s under SwiftShader. Determinism comes from the engine, and is verified by md5.
2. **Tone mapping moved into foundation's resolve pass.** Accumulation must be linear HDR and three disables tone mapping when rendering to a target. Consequence: `material.toneMapped = false` is **not** honoured — use emissive intensity.
3. **`cinema.buildPost` returns `Post = {render(scene,camera,target,t,dt,ctx), setSize, dispose}`**, not an `EffectComposer` — the accumulator must own sequencing. Fallback returns `null`.
4. **Added `cinema.apertureOffset(i,n,shot,camera,ctx) -> [dx,dy]|null`** — the accumulation-buffer DOF hook; engine applies a compensating projection shear so the focus plane holds. Without it there is no path to real bokeh.
5. **`registerCinema` merges `shots` per key** so a cinema piece can restage one panel without deleting the other nine.
6. **`--piece=<id>` = `PIECE_HEROES[id]` + every isoShot with `spec.piece === id`.** `PIECE_HEROES` is a frozen foundation-owned map so no piece edits a shared file to get a capture set.
7. **Concurrency hardening (not in spec, required for 16 parallel agents):** `startServerAuto` falls back to an ephemeral port on EADDRINUSE (5178/5179 would otherwise collide 16 ways), and `ensureBuild` takes a `.build.lock` file mutex with stale-lock breaking so concurrent `vite build`s can't shred `dist/`.
8. **Piece placeholders export `export const PIECE = '<id>'`** (spec said export nothing) — used for `--list` slot provenance.
9. **`progress/index.html` is generated** by `tools/progress.mjs`, one file that inlines a bootstrap snapshot (so `file://` works) *and* Range-polls `events.jsonl` when served. Only images referenced by events + all bar panels are inlined, so it stays ~3.6 MB instead of ballooning.
10. `shadowMap.type = PCFShadowMap` (PCFSoft is deprecated in r0.185 and silently downgrades).

### Frozen files — nobody edits these after now
`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `vite.config.js`, `index.html`, `compare.html`, `README.md`, all of `src/foundation/**`, `src/main.js`, `src/pieces/index.js`, all of `scripts/**`, `tools/progress.mjs`, `progress/index.html`. `progress/events.jsonl` is append-only via `scripts/log-event.mjs`.

Full contract reference, URL params, flag tables and the critic loop are in `/home/user/nflblitz/README.md`.
